title: Exact coherent monoidal evaluation at a normed-coefficient geometric point
statement:
Work in compatible small-site and coefficient universes [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $F$ be a normed field with totally disconnected metric topology, let $C_F(P)=C(P,F)$ on profinite sets [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], and put $F_T=p_T^*C_F$ for every scheme $T$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use internal $F_T$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], relative tensor [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor, def-sfb-modobj-symmetric-tensor], and the module inverse image $f_F^*=\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_{f,F}}\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(f^{-1})$ of [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback].

Let $Z$ be any scheme, $k$ an algebraically closed field, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and $x:s\to Z$ a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point]. Put $E_F(N)=\Gamma(s,N)$ and $\Phi_{x,F}=E_F\circ x_F^*$, with the abstract $F$-actions given by constant sections. The constant-section ring map $c_F:F\to\Gamma(s,F_s)$ is an isomorphism. The functor $E_F$ is exact and additive. The natural balanced map
$$b_{N,N'}:E_F(N)\otimes_F E_F(N')\longrightarrow E_F(N\otimes_{F_s}N'),\qquad n\otimes n'\longmapsto[n\otimes n']$$
is an isomorphism for arbitrary internal $F_s$-modules $N,N'$. Here the bracket denotes the sectionwise balanced tensor followed by its sheafification and the internal/sectionwise tensor identification [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The unit map is $c_F:F\xrightarrow{\sim}E_F(F_s)$. These specified maps satisfy associativity, both unit and symmetry coherence equations, and make $E_F$ strong symmetric monoidal.

Let $q_x:x_F^*(M\otimes_{F_Z}M')\xrightarrow{\sim}x_F^*M\otimes_{F_s}x_F^*M'$ be the canonical balanced inverse-image tensor comparison and $u_x:x_F^*F_Z\xrightarrow{\sim}F_s$ the canonical regular-module comparison from the coefficient isomorphism $\alpha_{x,F}$. The exact additive functor $\Phi_{x,F}$ is strong symmetric monoidal with tensorator
$$\Phi_{x,F}(M)\otimes_F\Phi_{x,F}(M')\xrightarrow{b}E_F(x_F^*M\otimes_{F_s}x_F^*M')\xrightarrow{E_F(q_x^{-1})}\Phi_{x,F}(M\otimes_{F_Z}M')$$
and unit $F\xrightarrow{c_F}E_F(F_s)\xrightarrow{E_F(u_x^{-1})}\Phi_{x,F}(F_Z)$. In particular these tensorators satisfy all the symmetric monoidal coherence equations and identify $\Phi_{x,F}(F_Z)$ with $F$. No constructibility, Noetherianity or completeness is assumed.

proof.text: The scheme $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ is affine, with one point and local ring $k$. A field is henselian (the maximal ideal is zero, so a simple residual root is already a root), and $k$ is separably closed since it is algebraically closed. Thus $s$ is w-strictly local, and its singleton component space is extremally disconnected. By the definition in [det-pe-wlocal-strict-contractible], $k$ is w-contractible. Apply [det-pe-wcb-projective] to $s$ as an object of its own pro-etale site: $s$ is weakly contractible in the sheaf-theoretic sense. Also [det-pe-wcb-clopen-partition] says every covering of $s$ refines a finite clopen partition. Since $s$ is connected and nonempty, its only nonempty partition member is $s$ itself. These assertions concern coverings of the terminal object, not coverings of every pro-etale $s$-scheme.

source.place: Lemma 4.1(1), w-contractible affine hypothesis; Bhatt-Scholze Section 2.4

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-point-basis-evaluation] with $X=U=s$ and with the condensed ring $C_F$. The canonical ring identification is $\Gamma(s,F_s)\cong C_F(\pi_0(s))=C(*,F)$. Evaluation at the unique point identifies the last ring with $F$; its inverse sends $a\in F$ to the constant map with value $a$. By the continuous-function definition [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], this inverse followed by the canonical coefficient identification is exactly the constant-section map $c_F$, rather than an unspecified abstract ring isomorphism. Thus $c_F$ is a ring isomorphism and the scalar action through it is the action required in the statement.

Use [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison] for the canonical exact equivalence from internal $F_s$-modules to sectionwise modules over the reconstructed ring sheaf $B_s$. It leaves sections and maps unchanged. By [det-pe-sections-limits-colimits], evaluation at the weakly contractible affine $s$ preserves all limits and colimits on these module sheaves. In particular it preserves kernels and cokernels, so is exact. It is additive because morphism addition and the zero morphism are evaluated sectionwise. Replacing the scalar ring $B_s(s)$ by $F$ through $c_F$ changes neither groups nor maps nor exactness. This proves the assertion about $E_F$ on every internal module, without a finiteness hypothesis.

source.place: Lemma 4.1(1), exact evaluation; internal/sectionwise comparison: Stacks Tag 03EK

proof.text: The small pro-etale site has pullbacks, a strict empty object and disjoint finite coproducts stable under pullback; coproduct component inclusions cover, including the empty covering of the empty scheme. These follow directly from the site definition [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]: take scheme fibre products and disjoint unions, and use their componentwise covering condition. Step 1 supplies the partition-refinement condition at its terminal object $s$, and step 3 supplies exactness. Apply [lem-zl-partition-section-tensor-flat] with $W=s$ and $\mathcal O=B_s$. Its canonical section tensor pairing is an isomorphism for arbitrary module sheaves and respects associativity, symmetry and both unit laws. The comparison of [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison] identifies internal relative tensor with sheafified sectionwise tensor by the identity on local pure tensors, preserving all these constraints. Therefore the resulting pairing is precisely $n\otimes n'\mapsto[n\otimes n']$, the specified $b$, after the ring identification $c_F$. The unit pairing, originally $B_s(s)\to B_s(s)$, becomes $c_F$. Hence these specified maps make $E_F$ strong symmetric monoidal.

source.place: Lemma 4.1(1), tensor sheafification calculation; Stacks Tag 0F63 and Tag 03EK

proof.text: Take $\Lambda=C_F$. The coefficient map $\alpha_{x,F}$ is an isomorphism for this arbitrary condensed ring by [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms]; this does not require restricting to the finite list of admissible adic coefficients. By [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-main], the specified $x_F^*$ is additive and exact. The comparisons of [lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport] identify it with the ringed-topos pullback $B_s\otimes_{x^{-1}B_Z}x^{-1}(-)$, through equivalences leaving underlying sheaves unchanged. Apply [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence] to that ringed-topos morphism and complexes concentrated in degree zero. Its pure-tensor maps are $(a\otimes m)\otimes(a'\otimes m')\mapsto aa'\otimes(m\otimes m')$ and its inverse, and its regular-module map is $a\otimes r\mapsto a\alpha_{x,F}(r)$. Transport through [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison]. This gives exactly $q_x^{-1}$ and $u_x$ of the statement; the cited cochain comparison includes associativity, both action unitors and signed symmetry, whose sign here is $(-1)^0=1$. Consequently the specified ordinary module comparisons give a strong symmetric monoidal structure on $x_F^*$.

source.place: Section 3, geometric inverse image; ordinary comparison: Stacks Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback

proof.text: Compose the structures of steps 4 and 5. The composite tensorator is, by its definition, $E_F(q_x^{-1})\circ b_{x_F^*M,x_F^*M'}$, and its unit is $E_F(u_x^{-1})\circ c_F$, exactly the displayed arrows. In the associativity diagram, move each inner tensor comparison through $b$ by naturality, then use the associativity equations for $b$ and $q_x^{-1}$. For the symmetry diagram use the same naturality followed by their symmetry equations; for each unit diagram use their corresponding unit equations. This proves each composite coherence equation. All the component maps are isomorphisms, as is the composite unit; its inverse identifies $\Phi_{x,F}(F_Z)$ with $F$. Additivity and exactness also compose. Every argument used arbitrary modules and arbitrary schemes, and none used completeness of $F$.

The statement and stmt_deps are unchanged. The statement is correct: c_F is F to C(*,F)=Gamma(s,F_s). HRS Example 3.1 (p.6) holds for T1 rings, which covers normed fields, and Lemma 4.1(1) (p.8) gives a t-exact symmetric monoidal RGamma on a w-contractible scheme. Nothing uses SGA, completeness or finiteness. Step 1: Spec k is w-contractible, being one point with a separably closed field as local ring. wcb-projective clause 2 makes it weakly contractible, and the clopen partition of a connected s is just s. Step 2: point-basis-evaluation with X=U=s. Its p_X^* is the same construction as sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point, and the identification is inverse to c_F. Step 3: exactness and additivity follow from internal-section-comparison plus sections-limits-colimits. Step 4: I checked every hypothesis of lem-zl-partition-section-tensor-flat, including s terminal, strict empty object, coproducts, refinement and exactness. Its tensor is def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, which is the item's bracket. Step 5: the item's x_F^* = Ext_alpha mapMod is f^*_int of the operations-transport node, and alpha is invertible for any Lambda. The cochain coherence node in degree 0 gives q_x with sign 1 and u_x as the unitor, with directions matching. Step 6 composes elementarily, and the tensorator and unit agree with the displayed maps. Site sizes: the wcb nodes use sk-def-pe-site rather than the U-bounded site, which is harmless for Spec k. A BFS over 591 dependencies finds no cycle. No duplicate exists: lem-weil-point-finite-free-sections-tensor and lem-pod-point-dualizing-complex differ. Accepted tool_uses: the nine declared generic nodes. No fixes.
